title: Surge Dry-Run: Fringe Region Observations & Quick Actions
body:
Date: 2027-11-02
Owners: Asha Kaur (note lead)
Attendees: Asha Kaur, Benji Morales, Claire Ng, Dmitri Petrov, Riley Chen, on-call infra
Purpose: run a controlled surge dry-run against a fringe/edge region to validate prewarming, batching, fallback, and autoscale behaviors before Black Friday smoke-testing window.
Duration: 20m steady-state surge window + 30m warmup/observation
Target region: eu-north-1-edge (fringe POP)
Test profile: synthetic replay of production traces scaled to 2.5x baseline QPS; mixed payload distribution (short chat 65%, long gen 25%, embeddings 10%)
Fleet snapshot before run: 24 x A100 (mixed 80GB/40GB), 4 spare nodes reserved, model pool: redwood-llama-13b-q2 + redwood-llama-13b-quant-v2 fallback

Summary of outcomes:
- Prewarming: prefix/KV cache priming lowered cold-start token emission latency significantly. Cold-start p50 decreased from ~410ms to ~110ms post-priming; p95 improved from ~2.8s to ~720ms.
- Batching behavior: continuous batching reduced CPU overhead but introduced slightly higher median token latency for short-chat requests (p50 +18ms). This is acceptable for most flows but flagged for product review.
- Autoscale: scale-up triggered at expected signal threshold but cool-down window caused delayed reclamation leading to 12% of requests routed to fallback model when capacity throttled.
- Fallback policy exercised: 12% of requests served by redwood-llama-13b-quant-v2; quality regression within expected bounds for embeddings, but chat hallucination rate increased on a small subset (~0.4% of sampled responses).
- Failure mode observed: one worker hit an I/O stall due to cron-based prefetch job not running (container exit/restart during warmup). Root cause: missing liveness probe config for prefetch job (ticket INFRA-3421 opened).

Detailed observations and notes:
1) Warmup effectiveness
   - Approach: streamed 10k prefixes aligned with top 50 user prompts, KV cache prepopulated across 16 host shards.
   - Result: cache hit rate improved from 27% to 82% for seeded prefixes within 8 minutes.
   - Note: hosts with older kernel (5.15.x) showed slower mmap-backed KV load; schedule kernel parity patching for eu-north-1-edge in next maintenance window.

2) Latency breakdown (surge window averages)
   - Request types: short-chat (65%): p50 130ms, p95 890ms; long-gen (25%): p50 420ms, p95 2.2s; embeddings (10%): p50 90ms, p95 380ms.
   - Token generation overhead: batching queue time average 12ms, serialization CPU 18ms, network hop median 22ms.

3) Capacity / throughput
   - Sustained throughput achieved: 2.3x baseline (goal 2.5x) before fallback activation.
   - Bottleneck: single-host NVMe write lock observed under heavy KV refresh spikes; plan to move refresh to off-peak microbatches.

4) Fallback routing behavior
   - Policy correctly tripped when queueing latency exceeded SLO of 1.2s for generation requests.
   - Edge case: split-horizon routing caused ~1% misrouted requests during short window; needs fix in routing table generation logic (PR: ops-runbooks#298 notes).

Immediate action items (owners):
- INFRA-3421 (Dmitri): add liveness probe and restart backoff for prefetch microservice; add unit test coverage for container lifecycle hooks. Target: 2027-11-05.
- (Asha): update surge dry-run checklist to add kernel-version gate for fringe POPs; link to patch playbook. Target: 2027-11-04.
- (Benji): tune autoscale cool-down from 300s -> 120s for edge pools; validate with local sim. Target: 2027-11-06.
- (Claire): add quality monitor snapshot for responses that went to fallback; create regression eval suite. Target: 2027-11-09.
- (Riley): investigate NVMe write lock pattern and propose refresh microbatch cadence. Target: 2027-11-07.

Follow-ups / next experiments:
- Next dry-run: increase to 3.5x baseline and extend surge window to 45m; include cross-region failover exercise. Tentative date: 2027-11-16.
- Introduce hot-spotting simulation (10% of prefixes account for 60% of requests) to stress KV eviction behavior.
- Validate fallback quality with AB test and telemetry tagging to trace user-visible regressions.

Risk register / open questions:
- Kernel parity across fringe POPs is inconsistent; mitigation required before larger surges.
- Autoscale cool-down tradeoff: faster cool-down reduces fallback but increases thrash risk when bursts are transient. Need policy tiering per customer priority.
- Cache prefill cost vs benefit for low-util fringe POPs — economics analysis needed.

Notes to self / runbook edits
- Add explicit step to confirm prefetch cron liveness before surge window start.
- Document fallback quota thresholds and add a visible SLO dashboard tile for percent-routed-to-fallback.
- Keep a small always-on warm pool (2 hosts) in fringe POPs for rapid absorbing of bursts; evaluate cost against fallback quality loss.

Appendix (raw traces & refs):
- Example trace IDs: trace-eun1-20271102-01, trace-eun1-20271102-09 (saved to /ops/traces/2027-11-02)
- Related tickets: INFRA-3421, INFRA-3418 (autoscale policy tuning), RUNBOOK-77 (surge checklist)

End notes: overall the dry-run validated warm pool + KV prefill as the single most impactful lever to reduce cold-start tail. The two highest-priority changes before next run are: liveness probe fix (INFRA-3421) and autoscale cool-down reduction.

Quick decisions made in-session:
- Approve autoscale cool-down change test on canary fringe pools (Benji).
- Proceed with kernel parity patch scheduling for eu-north-1-edge (Asha).

-- Asha Kaur
